source: GIZ (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit), Support of Regional Economic Cooperation in Asia (SRECA), in cooperation with MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture — គោលការណ៍ណែនាំអំពីការនាំចេញផ្លែស្វាយស្រស់ពីប្រទេសកម្ពុជាទៅប្រទេសចិន (Guideline on Fresh Mango Export from Cambodia to China), Final Version, Phnom Penh, December 2020, 67pp
text:
Guidance on marketing and buyer relationships for mango exporters targeting the China market, per the GIZ/SRECA guideline (December 2020 edition).

Know your buyers: successful exporters typically build direct relationships and ongoing contact with foreign importers/traders in the destination market rather than relying only on one-off spot sales.

Promotional materials: exporters are encouraged to prepare basic marketing materials — contact information, a simple company profile or catalog, a website or social media presence, and business cards — and to have these translated into the buyer's language (Chinese and/or English, in addition to Khmer), since language barriers were noted as a practical obstacle to building trust with Chinese buyers.

Market visits and trade fairs: visiting China to attend trade fairs and exhibitions is recommended as a way to meet buyers directly and understand market requirements first-hand. The guideline lists relevant China-based trade fairs current as of 2020: the China Fruit & Vegetable Fair (chinafvf.com, held in Beijing), the China International Import Expo / CIIE (ciie.org, held in Shanghai), Asia Fruit Logistica (asiafruitlogistica.com, held in Singapore, typically mid-September), the iFresh Asia Fruit & Vegetable Industry Expo (ifreshfair.cn, held in Shanghai, typically November), and Asia Fresh (asiafreshexpo.com, also Shanghai, typically late November). Exhibition dates shift year to year (and some 2020 events were postponed), so current dates should be confirmed before planning a trip.

Branding consistency: the guideline emphasizes that maintaining a consistent brand/trademark and reliable quality over repeated shipments helps exporters build a longer-term reputation and repeat business with Chinese buyers, rather than being treated as a one-time or unpredictable supplier.
caveat: This document is very likely the same GIZ/SRECA fresh-mango-export-to-China guideline series already represented as mango Source C in the knowledge base (processed in Batch 43), but this is a later, more complete edition (dated December 2020, 67pp, vs. the earlier-processed 53pp version with data through 2018). Some content below (market/policy context, registration procedures, marketing section) is likely NEW relative to Source C; other content (GACC protocol, phytosanitary basics, documentation) likely OVERLAPS with Source C. This has not been reconciled against Source C's actual files — a duplicate-check comparing this source (tagged G) against Source C is recommended before both are considered final. This marketing/trade-fair content does not appear to have been part of Source C's previously-recorded topic list and is likely new.
